results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

Audited all 47 aligned units, p01–p47, against the independent summaries in draft order: three introduction units, all eleven body sections, and three conclusion units match their controlling ideas. Attached tables and figures complete the terse comparison/setup paragraphs; the three-part introductory callout is evidence with a null mapping, not an extra spec paragraph, and all 48 original outline summaries are preserved.

Audited every unit p01–p47 and the outliner’s sole two_ideas flag: that flag concerns the deliberately multi-point opening callout, not an arguing paragraph. The resource and practice lists group examples of one purpose; p31 develops one feedback loop, p35 relates production responsibilities to the same coordination constraint, and p45 synthesizes the shared-understanding problem rather than opening unrelated arguments.

Every prose/list unit and attached callout supports the post thesis: p01–p03 establish or preview C1–C5; p04–p11 develop C1; p12–p21 develop C2; p22–p31 develop C3; p32–p35 develop C4; and p36–p43 develop C5. The diagnostic questions p44 apply C1–C5, p45 joins C1/C3/C4/C5, and p46–p47 apply and extend C5; the career-pipeline example, productivity caveat, DeepSeek analogy and internal links retain those functions rather than becoming orphan arguments.

Audited all 54 specified evidence items across p01–p47 against the actual draft, including six complete tables, Figures 1–4 with their captions, both callouts, anecdotes, quotations, telemetry, reasoning and the seven further-reading entries. The text explains the PR’s failed trust function, separates measured churn from the author’s interpretation, distinguishes temporal coupling, states both directions of the burnout loop, limits the production comparison’s team-size inference, and connects every seam/action to its consequence; the DeepSeek example is expressly an analogy about structure and expenditure, and the productivity caveat states why raw speed is insufficient. This assesses explanation and the preserved argument, not external verification of inherited factual claims.

Audited all 46 declared boundaries: 34 within-container paragraph transitions and twelve body-section/conclusion transitions. The prose carries the trust gap into brute-force costs, churn into the contrasting mechanisms and taxonomy, local reasoning into ownership and concentrated burden, explicitly retrieves whole-system dependence after the productivity caveat, and moves from the coordination problem to stable seams, actions, reflection and synthesis; p46–p47 also express the specified action-to-platform elaboration. The two local reader pauses recorded under flow_is_followable do not erase those expressed boundary relationships.

Both independent readers recover the problem–consequences–solution order across every section, explain each section’s placement, and retain the section order. Their accounts also recover the concrete-to-general trust and workload sections, the monolith comparison, individual/team grouping, small-team-to-larger-organization contrast, and principle-to-seams-to-actions response; both follow the ownership/burnout return mechanism. Apart from the two separately recorded, different local detours, neither reports a lost thread.

results.draft_locus: The Role of Architecture: Cooling the System Down ¶6
results.quote: We have already seen, at the model layer, that **cleverness in structure can substitute for brute expenditure of resources** — DeepSeek being the obvious example of achieving strong results without simply burning ever more compute and money.
results.finding: Flow reader 1, item 1, briefly pauses to determine whether the application/team recommendation has shifted to model design, because the different kind of structure is not described; the next sentence makes the analogy clear and resolves the interruption. Flow reader 2 explicitly finds the model-layer shift understandable, so this local finding has no independent corroboration.

results.draft_locus: Why Small Teams Fly and Scaling Stalls ¶4
results.quote: Production readiness adds a related challenge: a large majority of AI-built applications never make it to production, and the gap between "works on my machine" and "works for 10,000 users" is where most of them die.
results.finding: Flow reader 2, Issue 1, briefly loses the team-growth thread when production maturity and user count enter before the following sentences distinguish the dimensions and connect their ownership demands; placing that connection first would avoid the local pause. Flow reader 1 explicitly understands the distinction and ensuing bridge, so this finding has no independent corroboration.

Audited first uses and paragraph openings across p01–p47 using the spec’s recorded engineering/technology-leader and principal/staff-engineer audience context. The opening defines the Vibe Monolith, and the text locally introduces churn, SDLC, coupling, Conway’s Law, intrinsic/extraneous load, the burnout label, white-box review, MVPs, bounded contexts and golden paths; cross-links explain their relevance without requiring prior reading, and openings carry familiar trust, boundary, workload or governance concepts forward. Neither flow account identifies an unexplained term that prevents understanding; the DeepSeek pause concerns an analogy’s place, not a missing prerequisite definition.

Audited the opening callout and p01–p03: a specific trust-and-sustainability claim leads into shared human responsibility and a concrete roadmap anchored on the 17,000-line PR. The opening is not a placeholder, restated question, dictionary definition, broad historical preamble or book report.

Audited Closing Thought p45–p47, with To Probe Further treated as reference apparatus: the close synthesizes trust and concentrated responsibility, gives an already-supported action, and hands off to the platform question introduced in the response section. It neither opens with a stock conclusion marker nor unveils the thesis or new supporting evidence at the end; the platform hand-off is a bounded extension, not a grab bag of unrelated claims.

Closing Thought p45 explicitly joins the trust gap and the pressure on whole-system experts as two consequences of work that cannot be safely divided, explaining why architecture must make understanding and responsibility shareable. Together with p46’s targeted boundary review, this connects technical trust, sustainable human capacity and scalable ownership rather than merely listing earlier sections.

Closing Thought p45 returns to the opening trust-and-sustainability frame and the first body section’s year of work in one unreviewable PR. Its account of work that cannot be safely divided gives that original example the shared-responsibility meaning specified in the callback.

The introduction-only reader accurately predicts the oversized-PR trust problem, brute-force costs, under-refactoring comparison, monolith taxonomy, cognitive load, concentrated ownership, burnout, small-team limit, stable seams, Monday actions and diagnostic questions. The expected personal, assertive practitioner argument with a concrete example, conceptual comparisons and practical advice matches the body; the supporting telemetry does not turn it into the systematic causal study the reader correctly says the opening never promised.

The original AC-1 reader identifies temporal interdependence despite genuinely modular components and correctly distinguishes application/database coupling, static service coupling and release coordination. The original probe did not explicitly request the under-refactoring subcomparison; the same reader’s criterion-AC-1-supplement.txt independently supplies it as insufficient consolidation, duplication and missed reuse versus repeated agentic changes to foundational boundaries, APIs and data structures. Taken together, the unchanged original answer and same-round supplement cover the full expected distinction without uncertainty.

The AC-2 reader traces moving seams to repeated whole-system relearning and extraneous cognitive load, weakened team responsibilities, and concentrated maintenance/validation on the few fluent AI users who still understand the system. The answer explains that execution speed does not remove interpretation and coordination work, describes maintained output masking depleted reserves, and states the burnout-to-instability return path; its qualification that prevalence and causal effect size are not established preserves the article’s evidential limits.

The AC-3 reader names domain boundaries, API contracts and shared data-model structures, selects them by consequences for other work, and proposes writing the protected decisions where teams and agents read them followed by human review of seam changes. The reader explicitly preserves rapid internal implementation changes and understands stability as deliberate change control rather than a permanent ban.
